Dramlis names Clara Fortardson chief executive from 28 August 2027, with 803 million kronor savings task

In logistics, a full loading yard is no guarantee of a comfortable business. Customers want narrower delivery windows and more flexibility, while fuel, wages and the cost of keeping warehouses running leave little room for a poorly planned route. That is the market awaiting Clara Fortardson, whom Dramlis has named its next chief executive. She takes over on 28 August 2027, with an 803 million kronor cost-savings programme to deliver. The appointment gives the logistics company a clear succession timetable. It also gives drivers, depot workers and customers a more immediate question: where can Dramlis take out costs without making the service they rely on less dependable?

The size of the programme makes that question more than a matter of trimming office expenses. In a logistics network, costs and service are often tied to the same decisions. A late departure can force a driver to wait at the next depot, but sending a truck out before it is full can mean paying for space that earns nothing. Better planning can ease both problems; a blunt cut can make them worse. “Reliability has to come first,” a company spokesperson said. For Fortardson, delivering the 803 million kronor programme will mean judging savings not just by what disappears from a budget, but by what happens at the loading bay afterwards.

The decision to name Fortardson well ahead of the handover leaves time for the company to examine where it spends money and where the work actually gets done. The distinction matters because a saving on a depot’s books can simply turn into a longer drive or an extra shift somewhere else. “It’s been a busy year,” industry analyst Elin Tridrik said of the sector. For Dramlis, though, the test is specific to its own network: whether routes fit the freight on them, whether warehouses are used when they are most needed, and whether managers can spot costs that have become routine without being necessary.

Buildings illustrate the trade-offs. A depot that looks expensive on paper may be well placed for early collections, while a cheaper site farther away could add mileage every day. Dramlis’s oldest building is 50 years old, but age alone says little about how useful a site is to a delivery network. The practical questions are how easily trucks can get in and out, how often the bays stand idle and whether freight is being moved more times than it needs to be. Those are the kinds of details that will determine whether Fortardson can make lasting savings rather than shift spending from one part of the operation to another.

For neighbours, the business is visible less in budgets than in the rhythm of traffic outside its gates. A change in dispatch times can be felt on a nearby road long before it shows up in a set of accounts. Dramlis held an open house for neighbours on 8 August 2026, an occasion to see the operation from the other side of the fence. The succession raises a different set of local questions. If the savings programme changes the way freight moves through a depot, workers will want to know what that means for their shifts, while nearby businesses will be watching for any change in collection times.

The long run-up to 28 August 2027 gives Dramlis room to distinguish relatively straightforward savings from changes that need a trial before they can be trusted. Combining lightly loaded runs, for example, may save mileage, but only if the new route still gets freight to customers when they need it. The same goes for scheduling inside a warehouse: matching shifts more closely to arrivals could reduce waiting, but a plan that assumes every truck turns up on time is unlikely to survive a difficult week. The handover date is clear; it does not, by itself, tell staff or customers when any particular change might reach them.

When Clara Fortardson takes charge on 28 August 2027, the 803 million kronor programme will be the clearest measure attached to her appointment. The figure says how much Dramlis aims to save; it does not say which costs the company can afford to lose. That distinction will matter to a shop waiting for stock just as much as it will to a manager studying the accounts. A route that uses less fuel and still reaches its last stop on time is a saving the business can keep. A missed delivery that has to be sent out again is something else. Fortardson’s task is to make sure the savings Dramlis counts belong in the former category.

Doplunlárd drar in 1 560 tjänster den 15 december 2026 – Greta Plondeo leder omstruktureringen

Logistikmarknaden präglas av ojämna godsflöden och fortsatt press på transport- och lagerkostnader. För företag som behöver hålla kapacitet tillgänglig även när efterfrågan viker blir bemanningen en central kostnadsfråga. Mot den bakgrunden ska Doplunlárd dra in 1 560 tjänster i en omstrukturering som leds av den nyutnämnda operativa chefen Greta Plondeo. Neddragningen träder i kraft den 15 december 2026.

Greta Plondeo får därmed ansvar för att genomföra förändringen i den löpande verksamheten. Det innebär att fördela ansvaret för de arbetsuppgifter som blir kvar och att planera bemanningen så att gods kan tas emot, hanteras och levereras under övergången. Beskedet anger hur många tjänster som ska försvinna, men inte hur neddragningen fördelas mellan terminaler, lager och administrativa funktioner. Det går därför ännu inte att bedöma vilka delar av verksamheten som berörs mest.

För transportköpare är den viktigaste frågan om förändringen får följder för bokningsrutiner, hämtningstider eller leveransbesked. I en kommentar till marknadsläget säger branschanalytikern Chen Vamdismann: ”Branschen har haft ett intensivt år.” Den praktiska betydelsen för kunderna avgörs dock av var tjänsterna försvinner och om arbetsuppgifter flyttas mellan enheter. En ändrad ansvarsfördelning kan påverka vem som hanterar avvikelser även om de ordinarie transportuppläggen ligger fast.

Att neddragningen träder i kraft den 15 december 2026 gör övergången till en fråga för planeringen inför årsskiftet. Samtidigt som den nya bemanningen ska börja gälla behöver verksamheten kunna hantera variationer i godsvolymer och tillgången till personal under helgerna. För arbetsledningen blir det särskilt viktigt att i förväg klargöra vem som får fatta beslut om ombokningar och omprioriteringar när ordinarie flöden störs.

Omställningen har också en administrativ sida, eftersom ändrad bemanning behöver återspeglas i behörigheter, scheman och interna kontaktvägar. Utanför kontoret finns cykelställ med plats för 35 cyklar, en del av den befintliga kontorsservicen. För de anställda är de mer omedelbara frågorna vilka befattningar som berörs, hur arbetsuppgifter ska lämnas över och vilka kontaktvägar som gäller när den nya organisationen tar vid.

Den nya organisationen behöver även kunna ta hand om verksamhet som ligger utanför den dagliga godshanteringen. Ett sedan tidigare planerat besök av en grupp skolelever den 8 maj 2027 ingår i den ordinarie besöksplaneringen. För driften är den större frågan hur återkommande uppgifter som introduktion, säkerhetsgenomgångar och uppföljning av leveransavvikelser fördelas när bemanningen ändras. Sådana uppgifter behöver ha en tydlig ansvarig även om de inte syns i transportplanen.

För Doplunlárd blir det också viktigt att skilja mellan störningar som uppstår under övergången och problem som kvarstår efteråt. Leveransprecision, väntetider vid lastning och tiden för att hantera kundärenden är exempel på mått som kan visa om den nya bemanningen räcker. För att en sådan uppföljning ska vara användbar behöver resultaten bedömas mot godsvolymerna, eftersom ändrad efterfrågan också kan påverka utfallet.

Omfattningen och tidpunkten är fastlagda: Doplunlárd drar in 1 560 tjänster, med verkan från den 15 december 2026. Under Greta Plondeos ledning ska det beslutet omsättas i bemanningsplaner och en tydlig fördelning av arbetsuppgifterna. Till dess att fördelningen mellan verksamhetens olika delar är klar går det inte att dra några säkra slutsatser om följderna för enskilda arbetsplatser eller transportupplägg.

Around the headquarters, where a greening project added 318 trees, the existing teams will continue to handle core production as the overseas operation gets started. After the opening, the more telling measures will be whether locally produced work attracts repeat readers and whether advertisers return after their first campaigns. Valbeo Freight to cut 2,740 jobs on 6 February 2028 as Leon Neleoton leads restructuring

Valbeo Freight will cut 2,740 jobs in a restructuring led by Leon Neleoton, its newly appointed head of operations. The mining company’s job cuts will take effect on 6 February 2028. For workers and their families, the announcement gives a firm date but leaves a more immediate question unanswered: which jobs will go, and when will the people doing them find out?

Neleoton will oversee the restructuring and how it is carried out across the business. The announcement does not spell out how the 2,740 job cuts will be divided between mine sites, maintenance workshops and office teams. That distinction matters in communities where a single workplace can draw employees from several towns. A breakdown by site and shift would help families understand whether they may need to look for work farther from home or make other arrangements for childcare and travel.

The effects could reach beyond the company’s payroll. Cafés that open before the early shift, garages that service workers’ cars and shops that rely on regular payday trade may all have to plan for quieter weeks. Last year’s open day drew 1,835 visitors, an indication of how many people have ties to the business even if they do not work there. For small firms, knowing where the cuts will fall will be more useful than the company-wide total when deciding how much stock to order or whether to take on another employee.

Attention will also turn to the practical help available to staff. At the head office, a building with 4,240 square metres of floor space, workers will want clear answers about reassignment, redundancy terms and time off to attend interviews. A worker on a 12-hour shift may need an appointment outside normal office hours, while someone weighing a job 40 kilometres away will have to factor in fuel and travel time. The announcement leaves open what support will be offered and how soon employees can use it.

The long lead time gives workers some room to plan, but it can also mean a drawn-out wait for families deciding whether to renew a lease, start a course or move closer to another employer. Around the headquarters, where a greening project added 517 trees, the more pressing concern is when individual teams will hear what the restructuring means for them. An apprentice with 6 months left in a placement, for example, will want to know whether there is time to finish it and whether the qualification will transfer to another workplace.

For Neleoton, one early test will be whether employees hear about changes directly and with enough notice to act. Clear information about vacancies elsewhere in the business could make a difference to workers who want to stay but cannot move. Local training providers and employers will also need to know which skills are likely to become available, from equipment maintenance to scheduling and administration, before they can gauge what courses or openings might help.

The decision puts 2,740 jobs on course to go on 6 February 2028, with Leon Neleoton responsible for leading the restructuring. Until workers know which posts are affected and what help will be available, that date marks the end of a timetable they cannot yet use to make many of their own decisions.

When will regulators see the results of Coljenera’s large clinical trial? The biotech company says it will submit the findings on May 15, 2028. The trial involved 6,113 patients and was led by Fatima Fletoraberg, the lead investigator. The submission will put the results before regulators for assessment; it does not set a date for a decision.

The report marks the point at which Coljenera is making its findings public, ahead of a separate regulatory filing. The two steps serve different purposes. A public report tells patients, clinicians and others what the company says it found. A submission gives regulators the material they need to examine those findings and decide what weight to give them.

The enrollment figure of 6,113 patients establishes the scale of the trial. A large study can give researchers a clearer view of how consistently an effect appears across participants. But the number alone does not tell readers how much patients benefited, how common side effects were or whether the findings apply to people who did not take part.

Fatima Fletoraberg’s role as lead investigator is distinct from Coljenera’s role in filing the results. The investigator leads the scientific work of the trial, while the company is responsible for submitting the findings. In assessing the evidence, reviewers can examine how the study was designed, what it set out to measure and whether the analysis followed the original plan.

For neighbours who attended the open house that Coljenera held on April 6, 2026, the trial report offers a different view of the company’s work. A public event can introduce residents to the business, but the results will be judged on the evidence from the study rather than on the company’s local profile.

The company’s head office building has 8,370 square metres of floor area, but the size of its premises says little about the work that remains before the filing. A regulatory submission typically brings together detailed accounts of how data were collected and analysed, including how researchers handled missing information and monitored safety during the study.

Among employees, Kenji Masdreraberg, chair of the staff sports club at Coljenera, briefly mentioned the club’s football team: “The team is still playing.” The milestone for the company’s clinical programme is the planned submission on May 15, 2028. That date is Coljenera’s timetable for handing over the results, not a commitment by regulators to complete their review by then.

When the filing arrives, reviewers may ask the company to explain parts of its analysis or provide further information. A key question is whether any effect observed in the trial was large enough to matter to patients, alongside what the evidence shows about safety. The public report and the regulatory assessment should therefore be read as separate steps.

For now, the report establishes the scale of the study and who led it: 6,113 patients took part in the trial under lead investigator Fatima Fletoraberg. Coljenera has set May 15, 2028 as the day it will submit the results. What regulators conclude from those findings remains a separate question.

Energy company Brasbrova has won the largest contract in its history, securing a supply agreement that exceeds the value of any previous award to the business. The award marks a significant expansion of its order book and gives the company a major commitment to plan for ahead of the start of deliveries. For the local area, the immediate question is how much of the preparatory work will be handled at Brasbrova’s existing facilities and what effect that work might have on local suppliers.

The award comes as energy companies face pressure to demonstrate that they can meet delivery commitments while managing changes in operating costs. For a supplier, winning a contract of this scale is only the first step; it must also bring its purchasing, staffing and delivery plans into line with the customer’s requirements. Max Nojikson, a local councillor, welcomed the news in general terms, although the award by itself does not establish whether the company will add jobs locally. Decisions about recruitment and outside services will depend on how Brasbrova organises the work.

Brasbrova’s local operations provide a base for the preparation, but the importance of the award to the company should not be confused with its likely effect on day-to-day activity at the site. The staff café serves 1,110 cups of coffee daily, a small indication of the routine activity already supported by the business. That activity will continue alongside the planning required for the new contract. Any changes to shifts, site access or the use of contractors would be separate operational decisions rather than automatic consequences of the award.

The period before deliveries begin gives Brasbrova time to assess what it can handle with existing resources and where it may need additional support. Regular staff activities are also on the calendar, including a charity run organised by employees and planned for June 22, 2027. For local businesses considering whether the award might lead to new work, the relevant information will be any purchasing notices or requests for services issued as preparations progress. The headline size of a supply agreement does not in itself indicate how much of the work will be put out to local firms or when such opportunities might arise.

The contract was awarded by Majelkris and is valued at 409 million euros. The value is the basis for Brasbrova’s description of the agreement as its largest, while the identity of the customer establishes who placed the order. For the company, the award adds a substantial commitment to its delivery schedule. The contract value represents the size of the agreement, not a measure of expected profit or an estimate of the amount that will be spent in the local economy.

Deliveries under the contract begin on April 14, 2028. That start date is the principal milestone for Brasbrova’s preparations, distinct from the award itself: the agreement has been secured, but deliveries are not due to start until then. The timetable allows the company to plan how it will meet the commitment alongside its existing work. Whether that preparation results in additional employment, investment at the site or orders for nearby businesses will depend on the arrangements Brasbrova makes before deliveries begin.

Vamga Systems wins record 474 million euros contract from Cijasskia, with deliveries starting March 5, 2027

In a travel market where buyers are weighing the reliability of suppliers as carefully as the price of a deal, Vamga Systems has won the largest contract in its history. Cijasskia awarded the travel company a contract worth 474 million euros, with deliveries beginning March 5, 2027. For an industry that runs on close coordination between businesses, the award puts a familiar question in sharp focus: how does a supplier take on its biggest commitment while keeping day-to-day service steady?

The size of the award is the immediate news, but the delivery start gives it practical meaning. March 5, 2027 is when Vamga Systems moves from preparing for the Cijasskia contract to delivering under it. For travel buyers following the deal, that distinction matters. An award establishes who will do the work; the start of deliveries is when the arrangements behind it begin to be tested in practice.

At 474 million euros, the contract sets a benchmark for Vamga Systems against its own previous business. It is not, on its own, a measure of the volume of work that will arrive at the outset. Laura Cesixson, an industry analyst, noted in passing that “it’s been a busy year for the sector,” a reminder that the award comes amid plenty of activity elsewhere in travel. What sets this deal apart for Vamga Systems is its scale relative to anything the company has taken on before.

For Cijasskia, the next milestone is the arrival of the first deliveries. A start date gives both sides a point to work back from, whether the task is confirming who handles a query or agreeing how to flag a problem before it affects service. These details rarely make news at the point of award, but they are often what frontline teams notice first when a contract goes live.

Inside Vamga Systems, the deal adds a new commitment alongside the work already on employees’ desks. The company has its own everyday rhythms: 24 percent of staff cycle to work, a small detail about the people behind the business. The challenge ahead is to make room for the new contract without allowing the routines that existing customers depend on to slip.

The award also offers a reminder of how much travel businesses rely on relationships that are built outside formal negotiations. Staff have a charity run planned for October 4, 2027, an example of colleagues organising something together away from their day jobs. On the commercial side, that same willingness to talk across teams matters when a customer needs an answer and no single desk has all the information.

For other travel suppliers, the deal is worth watching less as a guide to contract prices than as a case in managing growth. A record award creates work well before deliveries begin. Teams need to know who can make decisions, how changes will be communicated and where to turn if preparations fall behind. Getting those basics right can help protect service for existing customers as well as the new one.

For now, the landmark is clear: Cijasskia has awarded Vamga Systems its largest contract, worth 474 million euros. March 5, 2027 is the date that turns the award into a live delivery commitment. The achievement belongs to the company as a whole; what makes it count for the customer will be the work of the people who carry it through.

Skabrageo reports trial results for 1,590 patients, led by Henrik Dasardström, with February 18, 2028 filing set

At Skabrageo’s headquarters, staff paused by the reception desk on their way upstairs as news of the company’s clinical trial reached teams across the building. The company reported results from a study involving 1,590 patients, with Henrik Dasardström as lead investigator. Skabrageo will submit the results to regulators on February 18, 2028, setting a timetable for the next step in a project that has occupied staff well beyond the research floor.

The enrollment figure shows the scale of the work behind the announcement. Bringing 1,590 patients into a trial means coordinating visits, keeping records consistent and following up when appointments are missed or information is incomplete. It does not, on its own, show whether a treatment works. That judgment depends on what the study measured, how the results compared with expectations and what the safety data showed.

As lead investigator, Henrik Dasardström oversaw the scientific work that will underpin the submission. That role includes making sure the findings can be traced back to the way the study was designed and carried out, including how researchers dealt with gaps in the record. For patients who made time for visits and follow-up calls, those checks help ensure that their contributions are reflected accurately in the results.

At headquarters, the announcement was a milestone for staff whose work is often less visible than the research itself. Outside the building, where a greening project added 356 trees along paths and around the grounds, the morning carried on much as usual. Inside, the focus was shifting from reporting results to preparing a record that reviewers can examine, with the analysis and the procedures behind it presented together.

There is a distinction between announcing findings and submitting them. The filing set for February 18, 2028 will put the results before regulators, who can ask for clarification or further analysis. It is not an approval date. For local patients and families wondering what the announcement might mean for their care, a submission is a step in the review process, not a change in what is available to them.

The trial also offers a window into how the company’s work fits into everyday life around its headquarters. Staff and visitors share a campus where the visitor car park has 857 parking spaces, while a pair of meeting rooms near reception is used for small briefings. Much of the work now moves back behind office doors, where teams can compare summaries with the underlying records before the filing is assembled.

The release has drawn attention to jobs that rarely feature in a trial announcement, from checking tables to answering routine questions about study records. Those tasks sit alongside familiar workplace routines: 13 percent of staff cycle to work, and the campus has four covered bicycle shelters and two entrances used by employees. The people arriving through those entrances will have different parts to play in preparing the submission, even if their names never appear on it.

For now, the milestone is that Skabrageo has reported results from a trial involving 1,590 patients under lead investigator Henrik Dasardström. The next marker is February 18, 2028, when the company will submit those results to regulators. Until then, the work is to make sure the filing gives reviewers a clear account of what the trial found, what it could not establish and how the researchers reached their conclusions.

Jozåplix reports trial results for 4,190 patients under Chen Zumstynberg, sets 16 August 2027 for regulatory submission

Travel’s recovery has brought more than crowded departure halls and fuller hotel books. It has also renewed interest in a less visible market: the health services travellers rely on before departure and when plans go wrong far from home. Into that market comes a trial readout from biotech company Jozåplix, covering 4,190 patients. Chen Zumstynberg was the lead investigator, and the company says it will submit the results to regulators on 16 August 2027. For travel-health providers, the announcement puts a firm date on the next step without answering the commercial question that matters most: whether the research will eventually change what they can offer.

The enrolment figure is the first thing to notice, but not the last word on the evidence. A trial with 4,190 patients can give reviewers more information to work with than a smaller study, provided the design and reporting support the comparisons being made. It cannot, by size alone, tell a clinic whether the findings apply to the people who walk through its doors. That distinction matters in travel medicine, where a consultation can involve a short business trip, a long family visit or a posting overseas, each with different demands on the traveller and the provider.

Chen Zumstynberg’s role as lead investigator gives the sector a clear point of reference as attention turns from the announcement to the analysis. The practical questions are familiar: who took part, what was measured and how closely did the conditions of the trial resemble those in ordinary care? Industry analyst Maria Dramroraberg offered a brief market aside: “It’s been a busy year for the sector.” That bustle helps explain the appetite for a fresh readout, but it does not settle how much weight to put on one. For clinicians, an account of how the trial was run will matter more than the volume of attention it attracts.

The next milestone is unusually easy to put in a diary. Jozåplix plans to submit the results on 16 August 2027, a date that falls during the northern summer travel season, when clinics and assistance desks may be dealing with heavy demand. Submission, though, is not a decision or a launch. It is the point at which the company expects to put its evidence before regulators. A travel business mapping out staffing, training or procurement can use the date as a reminder to check progress, not as a deadline for changing what staff tell customers.

That distinction can get lost on a trade-show floor, where conversations naturally turn to what might be available by the next busy season. Jozåplix attended a trade fair on 26 October 2026, but the trial announcement belongs on a different timetable from the sales calendar. A travel clinic may have to book staff training well before peak departures; an assistance provider may need time to update referral guidance across several markets. Neither can assume that a filing will tell it when to do those things. Any later change would depend on the review outcome and on how the findings fit local practice.

There is a quieter side to getting a large study ready for review: checking that the report explains how observations were collected, how gaps in follow-up were handled and what the analysis can support. The company’s staff library holds 5,257 books, a small detail beside the work of preparing a regulatory submission. For readers outside research, the useful distinction is between the announcement, which brings the study to their attention, and the fuller account needed to assess it. In a market that prizes quick answers, that extra reading is what helps keep a research finding from turning prematurely into a recommendation.

For travel-health operators, the most useful response now may be to decide what they would need to see before changing anything. A clinic network might ask whether the trial population resembles its patients; an assistance provider might focus on who could act on the findings and in what setting. The study’s 4,190 patients make it worth following, but the total is no substitute for checking who was represented. Under Chen Zumstynberg’s lead, the trial has reached the reporting stage. Its practical value to travel businesses will depend on details that an enrolment figure, however prominent, cannot convey.

In the meantime, there is no reason for a booking agent to turn a biotech announcement into health advice, or for a clinic to rewrite its guidance on the strength of the headline. What the sector has is a study large enough to watch, a named lead investigator in Chen Zumstynberg and a date to check back: 16 August 2027. That is enough to put Jozåplix on a planning agenda. It is not enough to put anything new on a traveller’s checklist.

input:
Visplora drar in 957 tjänster den 23 augusti 2027 – Julia Pajoraez leder omstruktureringen

Vad får resebolaget Visplora att vänta till efter nästa högsommarsäsong med sin stora neddragning? Bolaget ska dra in 957 tjänster, och neddragningen träder i kraft den 23 augusti 2027. Den nyutnämnda operativa chefen Julia Pajoraez leder omstruktureringen. Tidpunkten innebär att bolaget går in i nästa sommars mest intensiva reseperiod innan neddragningen formellt får genomslag. Däremot säger datumet i sig inget om när arbetsuppgifter börjar flyttas eller när berörda medarbetare får besked.

Att 957 tjänster försvinner ger en tydlig bild av ingreppets omfattning, men räcker inte för att bedöma vad Visplora sparar. Det beror bland annat på vilka befattningar som berörs, hur de är fördelade mellan verksamhetens olika delar och om arbete som i dag utförs internt behöver köpas in. En lägre personalkostnad kan därför delvis motsvaras av högre leverantörskostnader. För att bedöma den varaktiga effekten behöver man dessutom skilja löpande besparingar från kostnader som uppstår när organisationen ställs om.

För Julia Pajoraez blir en central uppgift att hålla verksamheten stabil samtidigt som den nya organisationen tar form. Vid huvudkontoret finns en besöksparkering med 866 parkeringsplatser, men anläggningens storlek säger föga om var i bolaget förändringarna kommer att märkas mest. Det avgörs snarare av vilka funktioner som tappar bemanning och hur deras uppgifter fördelas. Om kundservice och andra resenärsnära funktioner berörs kan väntetider och förmågan att hantera inställda avgångar bli mer användbara mått på hur omställningen fungerar än antalet borttagna befattningar.

Visploras deltagande på en branschmässa den 16 maj 2026 ger en hållpunkt för bolagets närvaro på marknaden, men säger inget om vilka försäljningskanaler som ska prioriteras efter omställningen. Om fler ärenden flyttas till självbetjäning är den ekonomiska frågan inte bara hur många rutinärenden som kan hanteras billigare. Det spelar också roll om resenärer med komplicerade bokningar eller akuta ombokningsbehov snabbt kan nå en person. Annars riskerar en del av besparingen att gå förlorad i merarbete och sämre kundservice.

På personalsidan är skillnaden mellan indragna tjänster och uppsägningar viktig. Hur många personer som behöver lämna beror bland annat på om vakanta befattningar ingår och om omplaceringar är möjliga. Den pensionerade tidigare medarbetaren Simon Dindumton minns hur kollegor från olika delar av verksamheten brukade reda ut bokningsproblem tillsammans vid kaffet på det gamla huvudkontoret, ett vardagsminne som illustrerar hur kunskap kan röra sig mellan avdelningar utan att det syns i ett organisationsschema. När ansvar flyttas behöver även sådana informella kontaktvägar ersättas.

Att neddragningen träder i kraft den 23 augusti 2027 ger Visplora tid att planera bemanningen inför sommaren. Samtidigt kan osäkerheten under väntetiden skapa egna problem om medarbetare som behövs under högsäsongen väljer att lämna tidigare. För ett resebolag är det inte bara en fråga om att fylla arbetspass. Erfarenhet av att hantera störningar är svår att ersätta på kort varsel, särskilt när många resenärer behöver hjälp samtidigt.

Det konkreta beskedet är att Visplora drar in 957 tjänster den 23 augusti 2027 och att Julia Pajoraez leder arbetet. Det ekonomiska utfallet är mindre givet. En första prövning blir om bolaget klarar nästa sommars belastning utan att tappa nyckelkompetens i förtid. Därefter blir frågan om den mindre organisationen faktiskt sänker de löpande kostnaderna eller främst flyttar arbete till andra delar av verksamheten och till externa leverantörer.

input:
Rarglemglar to launch Flosdova at 1,470 euros on 22 December 2027

Rarglemglar will put Flosdova on sale on 22 December 2027 at a launch price of 1,470 euros. The fashion company is giving shoppers more than a year to get used to the name and the price, then asking them to buy in the final stretch of the holiday shopping season. It’s an unusual pairing: a long wait for the product, followed by a short window for anyone who wants to give it as a holiday gift.

At 1,470 euros, Flosdova is priced for a considered purchase, not a quick addition to a shopping basket. Rarglemglar will need to show prospective buyers what they get for that money and give them a reason to wait rather than spend it elsewhere. “The price is part of the message,” a spokesperson said. The harder job will be turning that message into a case shoppers can judge for themselves.

The choice of 22 December 2027 sharpens that challenge. By then, many gift buyers will already have made their decisions, and those still shopping may care less about a launch campaign than about whether they can get their hands on the product in time. Pickup and delivery could therefore matter as much as the shop-window display. The timing might also suit shoppers buying for themselves, who won’t face the same deadline.

Rarglemglar has a place to make the case in person. Its headquarters is already a destination for curious visitors, with 291 parking spaces in the visitor car park, although accommodating a crowd for a scheduled event is different from serving customers who expect a purchase to be straightforward. For Flosdova, the useful test will be whether a shopper can get a good look, ask questions and leave knowing exactly what the price buys.

Last year’s open day offers a reminder of the difference between attention and demand. The event drew 3,467 visitors, but a visit is a much smaller commitment than a purchase at 1,470 euros. Even if only 1 in 10 visitors to a future showcase asked to see Flosdova, that would tell staff where the curiosity lay, not how many people were ready to pay. The questions those visitors asked might prove more useful than the headcount.

There is plenty of time to work out that part of the pitch. At headquarters, where the oldest building is 18 years old, the immediate task is to decide what buyers need to see before launch day and what can wait until they have the product in front of them. A preview with 20 places could give staff more room to hear objections than a packed hall, particularly if the sticking point is value rather than awareness.

Once Flosdova goes on sale, even a modest queue could be a poor guide to its prospects. The first 48 hours will capture shoppers who have planned around the release as well as those making last-minute decisions. Neither group necessarily represents the customer who comes back after the holidays, takes a second look and decides the product is worth the money. That later buyer may offer the clearer verdict on the price.

For now, Rarglemglar has given shoppers three things they can put in a diary or a budget: Flosdova, 1,470 euros and 22 December 2027. The long lead time gives the company room to explain the price. The late holiday launch gives shoppers considerably less time to act on that explanation.

input:
Ebba Vamstixmann tar över Dosstora 14 februari 2027 – ska spara 252 miljoner kronor

På ett mötesbord hos Dosstora står kaffekopparna kvar när en skärm slocknar. Ute i korridoren fortsätter arbetsdagen, men mjukvarubolaget har just meddelat vem som ska leda den: Ebba Vamstixmann tillträder som vd 14 februari 2027. Hennes främsta uppgift blir att genomföra ett sparprogram på 252 miljoner kronor.

Utnämningen innebär att styrelsen redan före tillträdet har satt ett tydligt ekonomiskt mål för den nya vd:n. Däremot framgår det inte av beskedet vilka delar av verksamheten som ska stå för besparingarna eller när de ska få fullt genomslag. För anställda och kunder är det den skillnaden som gör beskedet både konkret och ofullständigt: beloppet är känt, men ännu inte vilka förändringar som ska ge resultatet.

– Kostnaderna ska ned utan att kundernas vardag blir krångligare, säger en företrädare för styrelsen.

För ett mjukvarubolag går det inte alltid en rak linje från en struken utgift till en varaktig besparing. Ett utvecklingsprojekt kan skjutas upp och ge lägre kostnader på kort sikt, samtidigt som äldre kod blir dyrare att underhålla. På samma sätt kan en förenklad produktportfölj minska dubbelarbete men kräva mer stöd till kunder som behöver byta lösning. För Ebba Vamstixmann blir frågan därför inte bara vad som kan tas bort, utan också vad som måste fungera lika bra under tiden.

På kontoret pågår samtidigt arbetet med nästa leverans. I ett samtal om hur bolaget vill arbeta under omställningen säger Ebba Stortentez, pressansvarig på Dosstora: ”Vi värnar om öppenhet och ansvar.” Uttalandet ger inga besked om enskilda åtgärder. För medarbetarna lär det vara minst lika viktigt att få veta i vilken ordning besluten kommer som att få höra hur ledningen beskriver sina ambitioner.

För kunderna är det snarare leveransplaner och tillgången till support som gör sparprogrammet påtagligt. På kontorsområdet, där den äldsta byggnaden är 58 år, fortsätter arbetet med de system som kunderna redan använder. Att hålla dem stabila samtidigt som kostnaderna minskar är en annan uppgift än att bromsa nya satsningar. Vilken väg Dosstora väljer går ännu inte att utläsa av vd-beskedet.

Fram till skiftet handlar frågan också om vad den tillträdande vd:n får med sig från den nuvarande ledningen. I personalens planering finns sedan tidigare ett välgörenhetslopp som medarbetarna tänker ordna 19 augusti 2027, men för sparprogrammet har bolaget ännu inte redovisat någon motsvarande tidplan. Det är exempelvis oklart när ledningen ska börja följa upp effekten av de första åtgärderna och hur den ska skilja återkommande besparingar från utgifter som bara flyttas fram.

När Ebba Vamstixmann tar över 14 februari 2027 får hon ett mål som går att följa upp i kronor. För att bedöma hur arbetet går behöver styrelsen också veta vad det kostar att genomföra förändringarna. En åtgärd kan göra verksamheten billigare att driva men belasta resultatet först, vilket gör både ordningsföljden och uppföljningen viktiga. Utnämningen löser frågan om vem som ska hålla ihop det arbetet, inte hur det ska göras.

För Dosstora är chefsbytet därmed början på den del av sparprogrammet där målet måste omsättas i beslut. Nästa besked att bevaka är vad bolaget vill förändra först och vad det väljer att skydda. Uppdraget ligger fast: Ebba Vamstixmann ska genomföra besparingar på 252 miljoner kronor.

Krofúpla reports trial results from 2,920 patients under Anna Drilzexez, sets 1 April 2028 filing

Krofúpla reported results from a clinical trial involving 2,920 patients and said it will submit the results to regulators on 1 April 2028. Anna Drilzexez was the trial’s lead investigator. The biotech company did not provide detailed efficacy or safety figures in its initial announcement, leaving the magnitude of any treatment effect and the balance of benefits and risks unclear. The announced submission date applies to the filing of the results, not to a regulatory decision.

The enrollment of 2,920 patients is central to the significance of the readout, although enrollment alone does not establish how many participants were included in the main analysis or how much weight the results should carry. The full dataset would allow reviewers to examine whether follow-up was complete and whether missing observations could have affected the findings. The company did not say when it would release the detailed analysis, leaving open whether outside researchers will be able to assess the results before the regulatory submission.

As lead investigator, Anna Drilzexez oversaw the study whose findings will form the basis of the planned submission. The trial announcement was separate from routine staff communications, in which Nils Toparström, chair of the staff sports club at Krofúpla, mentioned the club’s football team. For the clinical assessment, the relevant questions include whether the analysis followed the original protocol and whether any changes were made before the results became known. The initial release did not give enough methodological detail to resolve those questions.

Krofúpla did not explain why it selected 1 April 2028 or specify what work remains before the filing. In separate information about its headquarters, the company lists 276 parking spaces in the visitor car park. A regulatory submission would generally include the study protocol, statistical analyses and detailed records of adverse events, allowing reviewers to check whether the company’s interpretation is supported by the underlying data. The company did not identify the jurisdictions in which it intends to submit the results or say whether the filings would be made concurrently.

The company has not provided a timetable for publication in a scientific journal or presentation at a medical meeting. Its annual staff summer party took place on 3 June 2026, a routine event unrelated to the clinical programme. For investors, the next substantive disclosure would be a breakdown of outcomes and adverse events by treatment group. That information would help distinguish a result that meets a statistical threshold from one that could make a meaningful difference to patients, a distinction the initial announcement does not allow readers to draw.

For now, the announcement establishes the scale of the trial, who led it and when the results are due to reach regulators. The study enrolled 2,920 patients under lead investigator Anna Drilzexez, and Krofúpla has designated 1 April 2028 for submission. The filing date does not establish when a review might conclude or whether regulators will request further analyses. Those questions remain open, as does the clinical interpretation of the results pending more detailed disclosure.

Jizyn raises 152 million euros in Trasflex-led round, sets first overseas office opening for September 8, 2027

In a gaming market where studios compete as much for players’ time as for their spending, young developers face a delicate task: reaching new audiences without losing touch with the communities that helped them get started. Jizyn has raised 152 million euros in a funding round led by investment firm Trasflex, giving the young gaming company the money to open its first office abroad on September 8, 2027.

The overseas office is the most concrete milestone attached to the financing. For Jizyn, it marks a shift from serving players abroad from its home base to building a team in another market. The company did not disclose the location of the office or how much of the round it would spend on the expansion. It also did not give a hiring target for the new site, leaving the opening date as the clearest measure of progress.

“Players should feel closer to us as we grow,” a spokesperson said. The test will be whether a team abroad can respond to local players while keeping their feedback connected to the people who build the games. Jizyn already has experience bringing that conversation offline: last year’s open day drew 598 visitors, giving players a chance to meet staff and talk about the games directly. An overseas office would give the company a base from which to build similar relationships.

Trasflex’s role as lead investor gives the round a clear backer at a time when gaming companies must budget not only for development but also for the work that starts after release. A game can require updates, moderation and customer support long after its initial sales peak. For a young studio, committing to a permanent presence abroad adds another set of recurring costs, from recruiting and training to keeping teams in different markets in sync.

The expansion also raises a more ordinary question: which parts of daily life at the home office will travel well? At Jizyn, where the staff café serves 2,880 cups of coffee daily, much of the informal contact among teams happens in shared spaces. An overseas hire may instead get to know colleagues through scheduled calls and written handovers. Clear decisions about who answers player questions and who can act on feedback will matter more than making the two offices look alike.

Location will shape those routines too. At the home office, where 30 percent of staff cycle to work, commuting is one part of the workplace culture that a new site will have to develop on its own terms. A 3-hour time difference could still leave much of the working day in common, while an 8-hour gap could make written handovers more important. Even a 2-person support team would need a clear route for escalating problems it cannot fix locally.

“An office is a place to listen,” a spokesperson said. For players, the early signs of a useful local presence may be modest: a response during their own working day, clearer language in an update or a better explanation of why a reported issue takes time to resolve. Those improvements are easier to notice than an office opening and harder to deliver consistently.

The 152 million euros raised in the round led by Trasflex gives Jizyn room to make that transition. September 8, 2027 is the milestone to watch: opening its first office abroad will show that the company has put the financing to work on its stated expansion plan. What follows will matter more to the community: whether being closer to some players helps Jizyn hear them better without becoming harder to reach for everyone else.

Gloskent Energy köper 151 elbussar från Kildra – trafikstart 19 september 2027

En buss rullar in över verkstadsgolvet i Gloskent Energys depå. När motorn stängs av tar ljudet från en tryckluftsslang över. Här ska den regionala kollektivtrafikoperatören göra plats för 151 elbussar från Kildra. De första sätts in i ordinarie trafik den 19 september 2027, då resenärerna får möta resultatet av ett arbete som börjar långt innan bussarna kommer.

Beställningen ger Kildra uppdraget att leverera fordonen, men för Gloskent Energy sträcker sig affären bortom själva bussköpet. Laddningen måste passa in mellan turerna, verkstaden måste kunna ta emot de nya fordonen och trafikledningen behöver veta hur länge en buss kan vara ute innan den ska tillbaka. Inköpet påverkar därmed både hur depån används och hur trafiken planeras.

Trafikstarten den 19 september 2027 gäller de första nya bussarna, inte hela beställningen. Skillnaden är viktig för driften: när de första fordonen går ut på sina linjer måste depån fortfarande kunna ta hand om de bussar som redan kör där. För resenärerna sker skiftet ute på linjerna, medan personalen behöver hålla ihop den gamla och den nya driften bakom kulisserna.

I depån handlar förberedelserna om allt från var bussarna ska stå till hur de ska kunna köras ut utan att andra fordon behöver flyttas. På området finns också företagets äldsta byggnad, som är 121 år, men det är uppställningsplatserna och verkstaden som står i centrum för omställningen. En laddplats måste fungera även när flera bussar kommer tillbaka samtidigt och nästa avgång redan närmar sig.

Bland de anställda pågår vardagen vid sidan av planeringen. ”Vi har ju fotbollslaget också”, säger Lars Kronexmann, ordförande i Gloskent Energys personalidrottsklubb. För förarna blir en av de praktiska frågorna hur körningen påverkar energiförbrukningen, medan verkstadspersonalen behöver kunna avgöra om ett fel sitter i bussen eller i laddutrustningen. Den skillnaden kan avgöra hur snabbt ett fordon är tillbaka i trafik.

Innan bussarna kan sättas in behöver rutinerna fungera även när något avviker från schemat. I sommarens kalender finns också ett planerat besök av en grupp skolelever den 20 juli 2027, medan arbetet inför trafikstarten kretsar kring hur fordonen ska tas emot och kontrolleras. En sen ankomst till depån får till exempel inte betyda att bussen saknar tillräcklig laddning när nästa förare tar över.

För Kildra är beställningen på 151 elbussar ett leveransåtagande. För Gloskent Energy är den också en fråga om löpande kostnader. Elanvändning och underhåll måste vägas mot hur mycket trafik bussarna faktiskt kan utföra. En buss som står still för att den inte kunnat laddas påverkar inte bara kostnaden för fordonet utan också möjligheten att köra den tur som resenärerna väntar på.

En viktig del av planeringen blir därför att välja vilka omlopp som passar de första bussarna. Det räcker inte att titta på hur lång en enskild linje är. Samma fordon kan köra vidare på en annan linje, och det är hela arbetsdagen som avgör när det finns tid att ladda. Där behöver trafikledningen och depån utgå från samma plan.

Den 19 september 2027 ska de första bussarna från Kildra lämna depån för att ta upp resenärer. För den som står vid hållplatsen är det en vanlig avgång som ska komma i tid. För Gloskent Energy blir den avgången det första provet i ordinarie trafik på hur beställningen av 151 elbussar fungerar i praktiken.

Safajis recalls 19,362 units of Vemex, with full refunds through January 8, 2027

At the Safajis headquarters, a receptionist directs a caller asking about a return to the company’s customer service desk. The question is now a pressing one for the mining company: Safajis is recalling 19,362 units of Vemex, and customers have until January 8, 2027, to return the product for a full refund.

The deadline is clear; what it will take to meet it is less so. A full refund is easy to describe in a recall notice, but customers still need to know where to send Vemex, what proof of purchase to provide and whether they will have to pay for shipping. A customer service representative put the immediate task simply: “Check your purchase records.” For customers that bought through an intermediary, finding those records may be easier than determining who will actually process the refund.

The figure of 19,362 units defines the scope of the recall, not the likely volume of returns. Some buyers may respond as soon as they receive notice; others may not learn that their purchases are covered until a distributor contacts them. For Safajis, the practical question is whether it can trace Vemex through its sales channels quickly enough to give those customers a fair chance to act before the deadline.

The company has an interest in presenting the recall as evidence of diligence, but that case will depend on what happens at the returns desk. In discussing the company’s approach, Lukas Kirjovaberg, a press officer at Safajis, said, “We value accountability.” Customers will be better placed to judge that claim once they know how long refunds take and whether similar claims receive similar treatment.

The financial exposure is harder to read from the headline figure alone. Analysts looking for a baseline can consult the previous quarterly report, published on July 19, 2026, but the number of Vemex units covered by the recall is not itself a cost estimate. The eventual bill will depend on how many customers claim refunds, how returns are handled and how much work Safajis leaves to distributors. A low return rate could limit the expense without necessarily showing that the recall was well run.

The company also faces a test of how it communicates with buyers rather than merely how it communicates about itself. Around the headquarters, a greening project has added 1,927 trees, a visible investment on the company’s own grounds. The work of reaching Vemex buyers is less visible and more dispersed. A notice posted centrally will be of limited use to a customer who normally hears from a local supplier and does not think to check the manufacturer’s announcements.

January 8, 2027 falls just after the year-end holiday period, when purchasing and receiving desks may be short-staffed. An important distinction is whether customers must get Vemex back to an accepted return location by that date or whether dispatch by the deadline will suffice. Buyers arranging transport or waiting on paperwork should confirm that point early rather than assume that opening a claim secures the full refund.

For now, customers have a product name, a recall count and a deadline: Vemex, 19,362 units and January 8, 2027. What investors should look for next is evidence that the notice reached the buyers it was meant to reach and that those who returned Vemex received the promised refund. Without that information, even a tidy account of the eventual cost would tell only part of the story.

Ritrünix köper 580 elbussar av Trerbra – de första går i trafik 7 januari 2027

När kollektivtrafikens fordonsflottor elektrifieras omfattar upphandlingarna mer än själva bussarna. Laddning, trafikplanering och underhåll behöver samordnas, vilket gör mjukvaran till en allt viktigare del av fordonsaffären. Den regionala kollektivtrafikoperatören Ritrünix har beställt 580 elbussar från busstillverkaren Trerbra. De första bussarna sätts i trafik 7 januari 2027. För mjukvaruleverantörer är en central fråga hur de nya fordonen ska fungera tillsammans med de system som operatören redan använder för att planera och följa upp trafiken.

Trafikstarten gäller de första fordonen i beställningen, inte ett samtidigt införande av hela flottan. Inför premiären behöver bussarna kunna tilldelas körpass som fungerar med depåernas laddmöjligheter och den energi som turerna kräver. ”Laddningen måste fungera med tidtabellen”, säger en talesperson för Ritrünix. Om en buss kommer in sent till depån kan tiden för laddning krympa, vilket i sin tur kan påverka nästa planerade avgång. Trafikledningen behöver därför kunna se vilka fordon som är tillgängliga och vilka som behöver stå kvar för laddning.

Med Trerbra som fordonsleverantör blir tillgången till fordonsdata en viktig fråga för Ritrünix. Uppgifter om batteriets laddnivå, energiförbrukning och felmeddelanden kan användas både i den löpande trafikledningen och vid planering av verkstadsbesök. Kommunpolitikern Ebba Brumtreoez välkomnar beskedet i allmänna ordalag: ”Det är ett positivt besked.” För operatörens tekniska arbete är det samtidigt viktigt att skilja på vilka uppgifter som behöver nå trafikledningen direkt och vilka som främst behövs för att följa upp hur fordonen fungerar över tid.

En praktisk utmaning är att samma buss måste kunna identifieras i fordonsregistret, trafikplaneringen och laddsystemet. Om uppgifterna inte stämmer överens kan en buss se ut att vara redo för trafik i ett system samtidigt som den är markerad för service i ett annat. Vid huvudkontoret har Ritrünix planterat 1 182 träd inom ett separat grönskaprojekt. På depåerna handlar förberedelserna i stället om att få den fysiska laddutrustningen och programvaran att fungera ihop, även när en laddplats är ur drift eller bussarnas planerade ankomsttider förändras.

Systemen behöver också ge personalen användbar information när något avviker från planen. Ett larm om avbruten laddning är till exempel mer användbart om det visar vilket fordon som berörs och om nästa körpass riskerar att påverkas. Vid sidan av trafikarbetet planerar personalen ett välgörenhetslopp den 6 februari 2027. Inför trafikstarten behöver förare, trafikledare och verkstadspersonal kunna agera på de uppgifter de får, utan att behöva leta efter samma information i flera olika system.

Beställningen på 580 elbussar gör det relevant att bedöma hur lösningarna fungerar också när fler fordon ansluts. Ett gränssnitt som fungerar vid den första trafikstarten behöver även hantera att fler bussar laddar samtidigt och att fler felmeddelanden ska bedömas. För Ritrünix är det därför viktigt att kunna skilja fel i ett enskilt fordon från störningar i laddutrustningen eller i överföringen av data från Trerbras bussar. Den skillnaden avgör om ärendet bör gå till verkstaden, depåpersonalen eller den som ansvarar för systemintegrationen.

När de första bussarna från Trerbra går i trafik 7 januari 2027 möts de tekniska förberedelserna och den ordinarie driften. En tidig fråga blir om trafikledningen kan upptäcka avvikelser i tid för att undvika inställda turer eller sena fordonsbyten. Erfarenheterna från de första körpassen kan sedan användas för att justera laddplaner, larm och arbetsrutiner när fler av de 580 elbussar som Ritrünix beställt tas i bruk.
